findings.title: Complaint directed into disciplined hope
findings.claim: At 12:86, Jacob's complaint carries disclosed inner grief toward one named recipient, and the knowledge he attributes to God keeps that disclosure oriented toward hope rather than family accusation.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers أَشْكُوا۟, بَثِّي, حُزْنِي, and أَعْلَمُ meet the independent complaint-to-God scene in 58:1, the grief-and-knowledge relation in 6:33, and the repeated knowledge formula in 7:62 and 12:96; the contact changes the complaint from an undirected outcry into a God-directed disclosure held by knowledge.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear complaint, grief, and knowledge as one disciplined movement that preserves practical hope inside the plain statement.
findings.containment: This retains the ordinary meaning that Jacob complains of his grief to God. It does not claim that the sons are formally accused, that every disclosure is hopeful, or that the excluded physical-spread facet of بَثِّي is active.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run publication is citable and trusted; its composite branch inventory is narrowed where the packet supplies counter-evidence, while the wider connections remain contextual retrieval evidence rather than independent lexical proof.

findings.title: Grief becomes directed disclosure

findings.mechanism: أَشْكُوا۟ supplies the voiced complaint and حُزْنِي supplies its heavy emotional object; 58:1 independently shows complaint addressed to God, while 6:33 joins grief with knowledge of hostile speech, making the focus's direction semantically active.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the destination phrase matters: it gives the grief a deliberate channel and keeps it from becoming a general accusation.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains Jacob's complaint of sorrow to God. The finding does not say that the family is innocent, that the complaint is resolved, or that every aspect of the root family is active.

findings.title: Knowledge carries hope through asymmetry
findings.claim: Jacob's knowledge from God gives the grief a surplus unavailable to the listeners, so the complaint remains capable of hope while still naming sorrow.
findings.mechanism: أَعْلَمُ and the following negated تَعْلَمُونَ establish the focus contrast; 7:62 repeats the same knowledge-from-God formula, and 12:96 returns to it after good news, making the contrast a wider pattern of knowledge that outlasts present absence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold grief and hope together without turning the grief into its opposite: what sustains hope is the stated knowledge asymmetry.
findings.containment: The ordinary claim that Jacob knows something from God that the others do not know stays intact. The packet does not identify the precise content of that knowledge, and no ranking between specific information and hope-grounded orientation is made.

epistemic.reason: The focus reader-walk support is legacy-unbound, while the repeated exact formula and later same-surah return provide concrete contextual corroboration without settling the knowledge's content.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how complaint remains disciplined: it releases what must be expressed without handing the grief over to the family's fatalistic framing.
findings.containment: This adds a pericope-level consequence to the plain complaint-to-God reading. It does not announce a surah-wide system, and it does not treat the later search command as content already spoken in 12:86.
